units.notes: marl, sand & gravel up to 25,000 years old

mostly fine-grained sedimentary rocks and volcanic tuff; lacustrine beds include marl & calcareous sand; the most common volcanic rock is silty and sandy tuff; other deposits include conglomerate and locally derived pebble beds; plagioclase from ash in mid-section 14.6 " 0.4 m.y. K-Ar; sample near the top was dated at 11.6 " 0.4 m.y. [see Miller & Schneyer, 1994]; 17.1 - 18.2 m.y. K-Ar

Thatcher Mountain Formation was named by Jordan et al. (1988) for this unit of sandstone and lesser dolomite, limestone, and chert; wave-worn debris of brachiopods & crinoids is common but not useful for dating; contains middle Wolfcampian fusulinids Schwagerina, Pseudofusulina, & Pseudoschwagerina

thin-bedded silicified siltstone and calcisiltite with very few bioclastic beds; contains middle Wolfcampian conodonts and fusulinids Schwagerina and Pseudofusulina; tends to accomodate deformation by layer-parallel slip and small tight folds; thickness uncertain due to faulting and folding

mixed terrigenous detrital-grain and calcite-grain arenites that are commonly burrowed; non-bioturbated beds have parallel- and cross-lamination; bioclastic beds are rare; contains fusulinids Schwagerina & Pseudofusulina? in its upper beds; Eowaeringella, Triticites, & Pseudofusulinella in its lower part

cliff- and ledge-forming fossiliferous limestone with interbeds of calcareous sandstone & quartzite; contains horn coral, Pseudozapentoides and conodonts Adetognathus and Idiognathodus of Pennsylvanian age
mostly shale & siltstone, but best outcrops are of rare quartzite beds; transitional member has limestone beds with Early Pennsylvanian conodonts
